financing.summary: M/I Homes funds land almost entirely on its own balance sheet: cash of $620.6M, an undrawn $900M unsecured revolver (PNC agent, matures September 2030) and just two unsecured notes series totalling $700M (4.95% due February 2028, 3.95% due February 2030). Homebuilding debt-to-capital was 18% and company-stated net debt-to-capital 2% at September 30, 2026; cash plus revolver availability ($808.9M after letters of credit) is about $1.43B (our sum, not a company-reported figure). It controls 48,934 lots, 52% under option or contingent purchase contracts with unnamed land sellers ($1.7B aggregate purchase price, $78.4M of deposits), and it developed over 80% of its lots itself in 2025. No land banker is named in its filings, and on the Q3 2026 call the CEO said the company does virtually no land banking and prefers to control its land, while conceding that perhaps it should have. Room for a land banker is therefore a greenfield conversation rather than a share-take from a rival: $1.85B of lots and land sits on balance sheet, the company keeps buying back stock ($250M authorisation, August 2026), and the $400M 2028 notes (callable at par) are the next financing decision.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning owner-developer. The 10-K states a target of roughly a three-to-five-year lot supply, acquired mainly through contingent purchase agreements and options with minimum cash down and takedowns where available; every purchase is approved by a corporate land acquisition committee. Over 80% of lots were developed internally in 2025. At September 30, 2026 it owned 23,425 lots (about 2.5 years, per the earnings call) and had 25,509 under contract, about five years in total. At year-end 2025 owned lots were 10,487 developed, 6,361 under development and 8,804 undeveloped. Land spend was $523.7M purchases plus $645.6M development in 2025, and $345.5M plus $413.5M in the first nine months of 2026. Management says it does virtually no land banking or other off-balance-sheet land structures, will not start selling land, and will be more careful on new deals.

land_banking.counterparty: Land sellers and third-party developers (not named)
land_banking.description: Not a land-bank programme: these are ordinary option and contingent purchase agreements for land and developed lots covering the 25,509 lots under contract. Aggregate purchase price is about $1.7B, backed by $78.4M of land purchase deposits plus $16.2M of letters of credit posted as deposits.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (filed 2026-10-23)
land_banking.note: Counterparties are described only as 'land sellers'. The company concluded it is not the primary beneficiary of any land-seller VIE; consolidated inventory not owned was $21.1M (down from $30.3M at 2025-12-31). At 2025-12-31 the 24,329 lots under contract ($1.6B) were scheduled to be bought from 2026 through 2031 (10-K). Deposit write-offs were $2.8M in the first nine months of 2026 and $11.8M (deposits and pre-acquisition costs) in 2025.

land_banking.counterparty: No land banker (company statement: virtually no land banking)
land_banking.description: On the Q3 2026 earnings call the CEO, answering a question on strategy into 2027, said M/I is one of the few builders that does virtually no land banking and was never drawn into off-balance-sheet structures. He prefers controlling the land directly, said the company is not paying a premium for that control, and noted its best deals are not exposed to a land banker's cross-collateral; he added that perhaps the company should have used it.
